title: Homoyessotoxin alleviates inflammatory responses by regulating the TLR4/MyD88/NFkappaB and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways.
authors: Gao, Xinyu; Chen, Kuilin; Wang, Hanyi; Guo, Yifan; Zhang, Ni; Su, Wenhui; Zhou, Jin; Xie, Weidong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究海洋毒素hYTXs的抗炎机制，涉及TLR4/NFkappaB等蛋白靶点的分子对接与动力学模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模无关。
abstract: AIMS: To explore the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of homoyessotoxin (hYTXs), a marine polyether toxin, by investigating its effects on key inflammatory signaling pathways and validating its therapeutic potential in vitro and in vivo. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Inflammation-related targets of hYTXs were predicted via network pharmacology, followed by molecular docking and dynamics simulations. LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were used to assess cytokine release, ROS production, and protein expression. Anti-inflammatory efficacy was further verified in mouse models of LPS-induced systemic inflammation and xylene-induced ear edema. KEY FINDINGS: hYTXs exhibited strong binding affinities with inflammatory targets such as TLR4 and NFkappaB1. In vitro, it significantly reduced IL-6 and TNF-alpha secretion, suppressed iNOS and COX-2 expression, inhibited LPS-TLR4 interaction and NFkappaB activation, and activated the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. These effects were partly reversed by HO-1 inhibitor ZnPP IX. In vivo, hYTXs alleviated lung edema, reduced systemic cytokine levels, attenuated immune cell infiltration, and restored vascular integrity. It also reduced swelling and inflammatory protein expression in xylene-induced ear inflammation. SIGNIFICANCE: This study is the first to demonstrate the anti-inflammatory potential of hYTXs through dual regulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NFkappaB and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways. These findings suggest hYTXs as a promising marine-derived compound for treating inflammatory disorders. Further studies are warranted to elucidate its molecular targets and clinical applicability in conditions such as sepsis and sterile inflammation.
abstract_zh: 目的：探讨海洋多醚毒素homoYessotoxin（hYTXs）的抗炎机制，通过研究其对关键炎症信号通路的影响，并在体外和体内验证其治疗潜力。材料与方法：通过网络药理学预测hYTXs的炎症相关靶点，随后进行分子对接和动力学模拟。使用LPS刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞评估细胞因子释放、ROS产生和蛋白表达。在LPS诱导的全身性炎症和小鼠二甲苯诱导的耳水肿模型中进一步验证抗炎效果。主要发现：hYTXs与TLR4和NFkappaB1等炎症靶点表现出强结合亲和力。在体外，它显著降低IL-6和TNF-α分泌，抑制iNOS和COX-2表达，抑制LPS-TLR4相互作用和NFkappaB激活，并激活Nrf2/HO-1抗氧化通路。这些效应部分被HO-1抑制剂ZnPP IX逆转。在体内，hYTXs减轻肺水肿，降低全身细胞因子水平，减弱免疫细胞浸润，并恢复血管完整性。它还能减少二甲苯诱导的耳部炎症中的肿胀和炎症蛋白表达。意义：本研究首次证明hYTXs通过TLR4/MyD88/NFkappaB和Nrf2/HO-1通路的双重调节发挥抗炎潜力。这些发现表明hYTXs是一种有前景的海洋来源化合物，可用于治疗炎症性疾病。需要进一步研究以阐明其分子靶点及其在脓毒症和无菌性炎症等疾病中的临床应用。
